prompt: How many $\frac{1}{3}$ cup servings are in $2$ cups?
hint: The question asks how many groups of one size fit into a total. Which operation counts how many thirds fit into the cups you have?

hints.title: 🔁 Another angle
hints.text: Use the "keep–change–flip" trick whenever you see division by a fraction.
The question asks how many groups of one size fit into a total. Which operation counts how many thirds fit into the cups you have?
Set up $2 \div \frac{1}{3}$. Each whole cup holds three servings of $\frac{1}{3}$ cup, so the division turns into $2 \times 3$.
$2 \times 3 = 6$, so there are $6$ servings in $2$ cups.

explanation: Finding how many $\frac{1}{3}$ cup servings fit in $2$ cups is a division: $2 \div \frac{1}{3}$.
Dividing by $\frac{1}{3}$ is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal $\frac{3}{1}$, because each cup holds $3$ thirds.
Multiply the whole number by the reciprocal to finish: $2 \times \frac{3}{1} = 6$.
There are $6$ servings of $\frac{1}{3}$ cup in $2$ cups.
